---
title: Development
---

## Layout

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `source/FaceView.mc` | View: awake / always-on switching, off-screen buffer, partial updates (MIP seconds) |
| `source/AnalogFace.mc` | Dial (ring, ticks, numerals, pilot marker), analog layouts, hands, analog always-on |
| `source/DigitalFace.mc` | Digital layouts, two-tone time, seconds, digital always-on |
| `source/TactixFace.mc` | Face `digital/tactix`: LCD time, seconds ring, battery, moon phase |
| `source/Hands.mc` | Hand shapes as local polygons, second hands |
| `source/Text.mc` | `TextKit`: system, vector (`Graphics.getVectorFont`) and procedural fonts (7-segment, 5×7 dot matrix) |
| `source/Fields.mc` | Data field slots (stacked, window, subdial, inline), edge gauges, status icons |
| `source/DataSource.mc` | Sensor and system data (ActivityMonitor, SensorHistory, Weather) |
| `source/Config.mc` | Theme resolution on top of the generated `ConfigBase` |
| `source/SettingsMenu.mc` | On-device settings (Menu2), driven by the generated `Schema` |
| `tools/gen_settings.py` | **Single source of truth** for settings → properties, settings UI, strings, `ConfigBase`, `Schema`, docs; `FACES` and `GROUP_FACES` / `SETTING_FACES` define the faces and which settings each one uses |
| `tools/setup_sdk.sh` | Headless SDK + device definitions + simulator font stand-ins |
| `tools/build.sh` | Type-check, `.iq` and per-device `.prg` builds |
| `tools/screenshots.py` | Simulator screenshots for this site |
| `docs/configurator/` | Web configurator: `render.js` (port of the drawing code), `app.js` (UI), generated `schema.json`, `devices.json` (`tools/gen_devices.py`) |
| `tools/apply_preset.py` | Writes a configurator preset into the property defaults for side-loaded builds |

## Build locally

```bash
SDK=$(tools/setup_sdk.sh | tail -n1)          # SDK, devices, fonts into ~/.ciq and ~/.Garmin
openssl genrsa -out key.pem 4096
openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -inform PEM -outform DER -in key.pem -out developer_key.der -nocrypt
tools/build.sh "$SDK" developer_key.der build check   # strict type check on representative devices
tools/build.sh "$SDK" developer_key.der build all     # build/OpenFace.iq + build/OpenFace-prg.zip
```

Device definitions normally come from the SDK Manager (Garmin login). `setup_sdk.sh` pulls them from the
public `ghcr.io/matco/connectiq-tester` image instead; with a local SDK Manager install, skip it and pass
your SDK path.

## Add a setting

1. Add a row to `GROUPS` (and an enum to `ENUMS` if needed) in `tools/gen_settings.py`.
2. Run `python3 tools/gen_settings.py`. The property, settings entry, strings, the field on `ConfigBase`,
   the on-device menu entry, the settings reference page and the configurator schema are regenerated.
3. Read the value through `cfg.<Key>` in the renderer, and mirror the drawing change in
   `docs/configurator/render.js` so the web preview matches.

CI fails if generated files are out of date.

## Screenshots

```bash
sudo apt-get install xvfb imagemagick fonts-roboto-unhinted fonts-nanum fonts-noto-core libwebkit2gtk-4.0-37
tools/screenshots.py --sdk "$SDK" --key developer_key.der --out docs/images
```

Each variant in `VARIANTS` is a patched copy of the project (property defaults replaced, clock pinned to
10:09:36, optionally starting asleep) run in the simulator under Xvfb. Garmin's proprietary device fonts are
replaced by open stand-ins (`tools/sim_fonts.py`), so text in screenshots differs slightly from a real watch.

## Release

Push a tag `vX.Y.Z`. The *Release* workflow builds `OpenFace.iq` and `OpenFace-prg.zip` and attaches them
to a GitHub release. Set the repository secret `CIQ_DEVELOPER_KEY` (base64 of the DER key) so that every
release is signed with the same key; without it, an ephemeral key is generated, which is fine for side-loading
but not for Connect IQ Store updates.

## Compute budget

| When | Work |
|---|---|
| Every second (awake) | Copy the off-screen buffer to the screen; draw the second hand (two polygons) or two seconds digits (cached bitmaps for Quartz / dot fonts) |
| Every second (MIP, watch asleep) | `onPartialUpdate`: restore the previous seconds area from the buffer, draw the new one, both clipped |
| Once per minute, on wrist raise, on settings or night-dimming change | Query sensors once (cached per refresh), draw dial, fields, gauges, hands and time into the buffer |
| AMOLED always-on (once per minute) | Draw the low-pixel face directly (no buffer) |

Hour and minute hands step once per minute. Only a *Seconds* field or a *Seconds* gauge forces a full
redraw every second. Simulator measurements (Forerunner 970, ms per awake frame): analog 25 → 15,
chronograph 45 → 16.5, Quartz digital 24 → 14, dot-matrix digital 118 → 16; what remains is the
full-screen buffer copy, which is much cheaper on watch hardware than in the simulator.

## Always-on rules

| Display | Sleep behavior |
|---|---|
| AMOLED (`requiresBurnInProtection`) | Low-pixel face only: outline/thin hands or hollow digits, ≤ 12 markers, no fills, black background, 9-step pixel shift per minute. *Full face* is treated as *Minimal + date*. |
| MIP | Full face, unchanged; *Always-on* and *Night* settings are ignored. Seconds via `onPartialUpdate`: the face is drawn into a buffered bitmap, each second restores the previous hand's clip from it and draws the new hand. If the power budget is exceeded, partial updates stop. |
